title: Nobel laureate John Jumper leaves Google DeepMind for Anthropic
summary: John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Demis Hassabis for AlphaFold, announced on June 20, 2026 that he is leaving Google DeepMind after nearly nine years to join Anthropic, calling DeepMind 'a special place' while saying he plans to take a short break before starting at Anthropic where his future role has not yet been disclosed; the move comes days after Noam Shazeer left for OpenAI and turns Anthropic into a leading buyer of AI talent, with a science-focused event scheduled for June 30.

title: Meta locks in 1.6 GW of Crusoe AI compute for Hyperion buildout
summary: Meta contracted to buy approximately 1.6 gigawatts of AI computing capacity from Crusoe on June 18-19, 2026, split across Crusoe data centers in Childress, Texas and Warrenton, Missouri with the financial terms and delivery timeline undisclosed; the deal lands in the same week Meta raised its 2026 capex guidance to $125-$145B (Q1 capex alone hit $18.997B) and Zuckerberg told investors that Meta Superintelligence Labs is 'on track to deliver personal superintelligence to billions of people' with Muse Spark already driving double-digit percent increases in Meta AI sessions per user.

title: DeepSeek closes $7.4B round at $59B valuation - China's biggest AI raise ever
summary: DeepSeek closed its first outside funding round on June 18-19, 2026 at more than $7.4B (~50B yuan) at a post-money valuation of $52-59B, with founder Liang Wenfeng personally contributing ~$2.8B (40% of the round) and Tencent, CATL, JD.com, NetEase and IDG joining; investors routed capital into a Liang-controlled limited partnership rather than direct equity, accepted a five-year lock-up and gave up voting rights, while China's National AI Industry Investment Fund got the only direct stake with voting rights - and DeepSeek imposed a strict no-poaching clause barring investors from recruiting its ~150 engineers.

title: Anthropic ships Enterprise-Managed Authorization for Claude MCP via Okta
summary: Anthropic launched Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA) for Claude's MCP connectors on June 18-19, 2026, the first live production implementation of the ID-JAG standard declared stable by the IETF/MCP on the same day; the feature lets enterprise IT admins provision third-party AI integrations once through Okta and push access to every employee on first login with no individual OAuth screens, with Asana, Atlassian, Canva, Figma, Granola, Linear and Supabase shipping support at launch and Azure AD/Google Workspace support on the roadmap.

title: Perplexity ships 'Brain' - a self-improving memory layer for its Computer agent
summary: Perplexity launched Brain on June 18, 2026 as a self-improving memory system for its Computer agent that builds a context graph of every task, reviews it overnight, and updates a personal LLM wiki that loads into the next session - with internal numbers showing +25% answer correctness, +16% recall and -13% cost on tasks the agent has already seen; Brain rolls out today to Max and Enterprise Max subscribers in Research Preview, and lands on the same day Perplexity added Deep Research to Computer with command panels, forking, inline actions, analytics APIs and custom credit limits.

title: Alibaba launches Qwen-Robot Suite as chairman Tsai bets on $50T full-stack AI market
summary: Alibaba unveiled its first Qwen-based robotics foundation models on June 16-19, 2026 - Qwen-RobotManip (a VLA model on Qwen3.5-4B), Qwen-RobotNav (a Qwen3-VL navigation model at 2B/4B/8B hitting 76.5% SR on VLN-CE RxR) and Qwen-RobotWorld (a 60-layer MMDiT video world model with 8.6M video-text pairs) - while chairman Joe Tsai told VivaTech the company is going all-in on chips, cloud, Qwen models and AI apps because AI 'could eventually create a US$50 trillion market'; the rollout was demonstrated on a Unitree robot dog and entered pilot testing with select Alibaba Cloud robotics customers.

title: Moonshot ships Kimi K2.7-Code with 30% fewer thinking tokens, ~$0.95/M input
summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K2.7-Code on June 16-19, 2026 as an open-weight, coding-specialized agentic model built on the same 1T-parameter MoE base (32B active, 256K context) as K2.6, designed for long-horizon software engineering and cutting average thinking-token usage by ~30% versus K2.6 while still scoring +11 to +31 points higher on K2.6 leaderboard benchmarks; the model is OpenAI- and Anthropic-API-compatible, slots into Claude Code/Cline/Roo Code/OpenCode with one env var, ships under a Modified MIT license with weights on Hugging Face, and lists at $0.95 input / $4.00 output per million tokens.

title: Meta launches $115M America's Workforce Academy to staff AI data centers
summary: Meta announced America's Workforce Academy on June 20, 2026 with a $115M first-year investment to train veterans, recent graduates and career changers as fiber technicians, electricians, welders and other trades workers building AI data centers - participants get tuition, airfare, lodging and a daily stipend covered and a job offer on graduation; the 2026 pilot runs in Louisiana, Ohio, Indiana and Texas with the National Urban League, Associated Builders and Contractors, CBRE and community partners, addressing the workforce side of Meta's $125-$145B 2026 capex plan and the same week Meta placed a 1.6 GW order with Crusoe.

title: Meta unveils Muse Spark from Superintelligence Labs - natively multimodal reasoning model powering Meta AI
summary: Meta released Muse Spark on June 19, 2026 as the first model from its new Superintelligence Labs led by Alexandr Wang - a natively multimodal reasoning model with tool-use, visual chain-of-thought, and a 'Contemplating mode' that orchestrates multiple agents reasoning in parallel; Muse Spark powers the Meta AI app and website today and is rolling out to WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger and AI glasses in the coming weeks, with private preview API access for select partners, and positions Meta against OpenAI, Google and Anthropic after a 33% Q1 revenue jump and a $125B-$145B full-year CapEx guidance.

title: OpenAI quietly A/B-tests GPT-5.6 Pro in ChatGPT - June 25 launch planned
summary: OpenAI is stealth-testing GPT-5.6 Pro inside ChatGPT, swapped in for some users who select GPT-5.5 Pro, with AI influencers citing 'unnamed sources' on X about a planned public launch on Thursday June 25 - and Polymarket traders pricing the June 22-28 launch window at 89%; OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki told staff the next model is a 'meaningful improvement' over GPT-5.5 per The Information, leakers claim a December 2025 knowledge cutoff, sharper reasoning (one tester said GPT-5.6 Pro 'continues to mog Anthropic's Fable 5 in 3D'), and SVG/3D design generation strong enough to beat peers.

title: OpenAI ships Codex Record & Replay - 'show it once, skip the script' on macOS
summary: OpenAI added Record & Replay to its Codex macOS app on June 18, 2026 (shipped in Codex app 26.616) and drew broad coverage on June 19-20 as a way for users to perform a workflow once while Codex watches, then converts that demo into a reusable skill the agent can execute on demand - bridging prompt engineering and automation; the feature is available today to ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise/Edu subscribers outside the EEA, UK and Switzerland, requires Computer Use to be enabled, runs on macOS only at launch, and arrives as OpenAI's EU AI Act Article 50 obligations are 44 days from taking effect on August 2.

title: OpenAI adds spend controls and unified analytics to ChatGPT Enterprise
summary: OpenAI added spend controls and expanded usage analytics for ChatGPT Enterprise on June 19, 2026, giving Global Admins a unified dashboard of ChatGPT and Codex credit consumption across users, products and models with the ability to set budgets and track AI spend by team; the launch also lands on the same day Computerworld profiled the new 'Global Admin Console' - but analysts cautioned OpenAI still cannot show how those costs lead to business benefits, so admins get cost visibility without ROI tracking as enterprise AI deployments scale.

title: OpenAI releases LifeSciBench - 750 expert-written life-science tasks for agentic AI
summary: OpenAI released LifeSciBench on June 19-20, 2026 as the first expert-written benchmark for measuring agentic AI on real-world life-science research rather than narrow biology trivia, with 750 tasks across seven core research workflows created and reviewed by 173 PhD-level scientists from biotech and pharma; the benchmark grades responses on scientific accuracy, practical research usefulness and adherence to expert collaboration norms rather than just a correct final answer, and lands in the same week OpenAI published a paper showing a GPT-5.4 agent on Molecule.one's Maria platform improved Chan-Lam coupling yields by >80%.

title: Anthropic ships Artifacts for Claude Code - live, shareable web pages from coding sessions
summary: Anthropic launched Artifacts for Claude Code on June 18, 2026 as a beta for Claude Team and Enterprise customers, letting engineers turn an entire coding-session context (code, tools, chat history) into a live, interactive, shareable HTML page that updates in real time as Claude modifies it and ships with version history and organization-scoped access control; Claude Code lead Boris Cherny called it 'a game changer' and Anthropic positions it as a bridge between engineers and non-technical stakeholders for incident timelines, PR walkthroughs, license audits and architecture overviews - and by June 19 it was topping Product Hunt's daily AI leaderboard.

title: Google DeepMind publishes 'AI Control Roadmap' - treats rogue agents as insider threats, runs on Gemini Spark
summary: Google DeepMind published its 'AI Control Roadmap' on June 18, 2026, treating advanced internal AI agents as potential insider threats modeled via an AI-adapted MITRE ATT&CK framework, with detection tiers D1-D4 and response tiers R1-R3, plus 'supervisor' models that review reasoning, plans, and actions in real time; analysis of 1M coding-agent tasks showed most flagged events stem from misinterpretation or overeagerness, not adversarial intent, and the framework already runs as a live monitor for the Gemini Spark coding agent, accompanied by a 'Three Layers of Agentic Security' paper aimed at policymakers.

title: Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer leaves Google to join OpenAI
summary: Noam Shazeer - VP of engineering at Google and co-lead of Gemini, who returned to Google in August 2024 from Character.ai - announced on X on the evening of June 17, 2026 that he is leaving the company to join OpenAI, with Google thanking him for 'meaningful contributions' to Gemini; the departure is one of the highest-profile AI-researcher moves of the year and removes one of the two named technical leads of Google's flagship model family as OpenAI ramps its post-S-1 hiring push, and is followed days later by Nobel laureate John Jumper's move from DeepMind to Anthropic.

title: Google opens pre-orders for $99.99 Google Home Speaker - first device built for Gemini for Home
summary: Google opened pre-orders on June 17, 2026 for the Google Home Speaker at $99.99 ahead of a June 25-29 ship date, its first audio device built for Gemini for Home and first standalone smart speaker since the Nest Audio in 2020; the speaker supports natural multi-step requests, 'Continued Conversation' in all supported languages, 10 new voices, two-speaker stereo and TV-Streamer pairing, Matter and Thread Border Router support, and an optional Google Home Premium subscription ($10/month) that unlocks Gemini Live, Camera History Search and Home Brief.

title: Meta rolls out AI Mode globally on Facebook Search - powered by Muse Spark, scrapes public posts for answers
summary: Meta's AI Mode went live globally on Facebook Search on June 18, 2026 (a soft-launch from June 15), replacing link-based results with AI-synthesized answers grounded in public posts, Groups, Reels and Marketplace listings and powered by the new Muse Spark model; the rollout covers trip-planning and product-discovery queries, gives Marketplace listings new visibility in answers, and warns that public content trains Meta's AI unless users opt out via Facebook privacy settings - the launch is expected to drive roughly 1.3T annual queries and around $15B in incremental ad revenue.

title: xAI launches Grok for Word add-in - drafts, restructures, and pulls web research into Microsoft 365
summary: xAI released the Grok add-in for Microsoft Word on June 18, 2026 (with PowerPoint and Excel versions already live since June 16), free for Microsoft 365 users via the Microsoft Marketplace; the add-in transforms rough notes into structured long-form text, fixes grammar in place with visible revisions, normalizes heading case and terminology across long documents, and can pull live web or X research, draft from recent emails and SharePoint/Google Drive files, and generate diagrams - extending xAI's enterprise push that already includes Grok 4.3 on Amazon Bedrock and Databricks Agent Bricks.

title: NVIDIA's ENPIRE lets AI coding agents run real-robot research end-to-end, hits 99% on Push-T
summary: NVIDIA, Carnegie Mellon and UC Berkeley published ENPIRE on June 17, 2026 - the first documented 'physical autoresearch' system in which frontier coding agents (Codex with GPT-5.5, Claude Code with Opus 4.7, Kimi Code with K2.6) autonomously reset, run and verify real-world robot trials and rewrite code; across eight dual-arm YAM stations, agent teams hit 99% pass@8 success on Push-T, pin insertion, and zip-tie cutting, with the eight-station fleet cutting Push-T time-to-success from ~5h to ~2h and pin insertion from 90+ min to ~40 min, and an open-source release planned.

title: DeepSeek releases V4 preview - 1M-token context, Pro and Flash tiers, native vision, Microsoft hosting it
summary: DeepSeek released preview versions of DeepSeek-V4 on June 18, 2026, more than a year after the original DeepSeek shock, with two variants - DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T parameters, 49B active per token) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B, 13B active) - both shipped under the MIT license with a 1M-token context window; on world-knowledge benchmarks the company says V4-Pro 'significantly leads' open-source peers and trails only Google's Gemini-Pro-3.1 among closed models, and Microsoft told Axios on the same day it is evaluating a fine-tuned V4 to power a low-cost tier of Copilot Cowork hosted on Azure.

title: Mistral ships Mistral 3 family - 675B Large 3 MoE + Ministral 3 edge models, all under Apache 2.0
summary: Mistral released Mistral 3 on June 18, 2026, the largest permissively-licensed model family to date, headlined by Mistral Large 3 - a sparse mixture-of-experts with 41B active parameters, 675B total, and a 1M-context NVFP4 format - plus three Ministral 3 edge models at 3B, 8B and 14B with multimodal base, instruct and reasoning variants, all under Apache 2.0; the release is available today across Mistral AI Studio, Amazon Bedrock, Azure Foundry, Hugging Face, Modal, IBM WatsonX, OpenRouter, Fireworks, Unsloth AI and Together AI, with NVIDIA NIM and AWS SageMaker coming soon.

title: Z.ai open-sources GLM-5.2 under MIT with 753B params, 1M context, $1.4 input / $4.4 output per million tokens
summary: Z.ai (formerly Zhipu AI) released GLM-5.2 under the MIT license on June 17, 2026 with full weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope, no regional restrictions and no strings attached - one of the largest fully-open flagship models of the year at 753B parameters (40B active MoE), 1M-token context, max 128K output, and pricing of $1.4 input / $4.4 output per million tokens (1/4 to 1/6 of comparable closed models); on the published scorecard GLM-5.2 beats GPT-5.5 on SWE-bench Pro (62.1 vs 58.6) and FrontierSWE (74.4 vs 72.6), places first on Design Arena, and is the first open-weight model over 80% on Terminal-Bench, with a new IndexShare technique cutting per-token compute 2.9x at 1M context.

title: MiniMax releases M3 open weights and arXiv paper - takes top open-weight spot on Artificial Analysis (55)
summary: MiniMax fulfilled its June 1 launch commitment on June 18, 2026 by publishing M3's full open weights on Hugging Face and the arXiv technical report (arXiv:2606.13392) describing MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA), which delivers more than 9x prefill and 15x decoding speedups at 1M-token context versus M2 at 1/20th the per-token compute; independent evaluator Artificial Analysis confirmed M3 ranks first among open-weight models on the Intelligence Index with a score of 55, with native image and video input and 70.06% on OSWorld-Verified for computer use, ahead of every self-hostable rival and several proprietary models.
